about.title: What the Parser Hears — measured pitfall matrix
about.as_of: 2026-10-08 (package versions pinned to what was current on that date)
about.value_encoding:
every leaf is "<native type>:<repr>", e.g. "bool:False" (Python),
"boolean:false" (JS), "Bool:false" (Rust serde), "bool:false" (Go). Maps with only string keys
are JSON objects in the order the parser returned them (Go maps are unordered; the Go probe
sorts keys; Rust serde_json/toml maps are BTreeMaps and come back sorted). Maps with any
non-string key are {"__pairs__": [[key, value], ...]}.
about.heard: per case, parsers grouped by what they heard: types normalised (str/bool/num/null), numbers canonical (1000.0 == 1000; an integral IEEE double is shown as the exact integer it holds, so JS's 12345678901234567000 and Go's 1.2345678901234567e+19 are both 12345678901234567168), map keys sorted unless order is the point of the case; date-times keep their native type
about.text_decoding: Python: bytes.decode('utf-8') (keeps a BOM); Node: Buffer.toString('utf8') == readFileSync(p,'utf8') (keeps a BOM); Rust: String::from_utf8 (keeps a BOM); Go and jq: raw bytes
about.nondeterminism: timings, bomb load_ms and the C-stack-bound depth limits (py:json, py:pyyaml.CSafeLoader) vary between runs; go:encoding/json/v2 error text picks 'cannot' or 'unable to' at random per process by design (Go 1.27.2 src/encoding/json/v2/errors.go:322-333) and is recorded as '{cannot|unable to}'

go:encoding/json.call: json.Unmarshal(b, &v) with v any (v1 API; Go 1.27 runs it on the v2 engine)

go:sigs.k8s.io/yaml.call: yaml.Unmarshal(b, &v) with v any (YAML->JSON->encoding/json, as Kubernetes does)

js:jsonc-parser.call: parse(text, errors) with default options; ok=false if errors[] non-empty (value still returned)

rs:serde_json.call: serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(text) (default features: Map is a BTreeMap, keys come back sorted)

# review-bot: agent service configuration
# Owner: platform team. Reload with SIGHUP.

schema_version: 3
service: review-bot
environment: production
deployed_at: 2026-10-08T09:30:00Z
regions: [eu-west-1, us-east-1]

model:
  provider: example-ai
  name: large-2026-09
  max_tokens: 8192  # hard cap per response
  temperature: 0.2
  fallbacks: [medium-2026-09, small-2026-06]

timeouts:
  connect_ms: 2500
  request_s: 120.0
  idle_s: 900  # close idle MCP sessions after 15 min

retry:
  attempts: 4
  backoff: exponential
  jitter: true
  retry_on: [429, 500, 502, 503]

routing:
  allowed_countries: [GB, IE, FR, DE, NO, SE]

prompt:
  system: |
    You are a careful code reviewer.
    Explain each finding in one sentence — cite the file and line.
    Never approve a change you have not read.

logging:
  level: info
  format: json
  redact: [GITHUB_TOKEN, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN]

budget:
  max_usd_per_day: 250.0
  alert_at: [0.5, 0.8, 0.95]

# MCP servers, started in this order
mcp_servers:
  - name: github
    command: npx
    args: [-y, "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
    enabled: true
    env:
      GITHUB_TOKEN: ${GITHUB_TOKEN}
      GITHUB_API_URL: https://api.github.com
  - name: filesystem
    command: npx
    args: [-y, "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", /srv/repos]
    enabled: true
    env: {}
  - name: slack
    command: uvx
    args: [mcp-server-slack]
    enabled: false  # waiting on workspace approval
    env:
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}
      SLACK_TEAM_ID: T0123456

cases.input:
# review-bot: agent service configuration
# Owner: platform team. Reload with SIGHUP.

schema_version = 3
service = "review-bot"
environment = "production"
deployed_at = 2026-10-08T09:30:00Z
regions = ["eu-west-1", "us-east-1"]

[model]
provider = "example-ai"
name = "large-2026-09"
max_tokens = 8192  # hard cap per response
temperature = 0.2
fallbacks = ["medium-2026-09", "small-2026-06"]

[timeouts]
connect_ms = 2500
request_s = 120.0
idle_s = 900  # close idle MCP sessions after 15 min

[retry]
attempts = 4
backoff = "exponential"
jitter = true
retry_on = [429, 500, 502, 503]

[routing]
allowed_countries = ["GB", "IE", "FR", "DE", "NO", "SE"]

[prompt]
system = """
You are a careful code reviewer.
Explain each finding in one sentence — cite the file and line.
Never approve a change you have not read.
"""

[logging]
level = "info"
format = "json"
redact = ["GITHUB_TOKEN", "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"]

[budget]
max_usd_per_day = 250.0
alert_at = [0.5, 0.8, 0.95]

# MCP servers, started in this order
[[mcp_servers]]
name = "github"
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
enabled = true
env = { GITHUB_TOKEN = "${GITHUB_TOKEN}", GITHUB_API_URL = "https://api.github.com" }

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "filesystem"
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/srv/repos"]
enabled = true
env = {}

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "slack"
command = "uvx"
args = ["mcp-server-slack"]
enabled = false  # waiting on workspace approval
env = { SLACK_BOT_TOKEN = "${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}", SLACK_TEAM_ID = "T0123456" }

go:yaml.v3.alias: alias-ratio heuristic, >100 aliases and >1000 decodes, allowed ratio 0.99 falling to 0.10 between 400,000 and 4,000,000 decodes: gopkg.in/yaml.v3@v3.0.1/decode.go:458-491

jq.depth: 10000 ('Exceeds depth limit for parsing'; MAX_PARSING_DEPTH in jq's src/jv_parse.c, see json dossier)

cross_format.timing_method: median of 501 parses after 50 warm-up parses, in process, monotonic clock (Python perf_counter_ns, Node hrtime.bigint, Rust Instant, Go time.Now); parse only, default options, untyped target; 3 significant digits; GC left on; jq not timed (process start dominates)

timing_contention.note: the parsers are timed one at a time on one thread (about 1 CPU of the cgroup's 2-CPU quota, plus GC helper threads in Go and V8); cgroup_cpu_used_s well above timing_phase_wall_s, or a large throttled fraction, means other processes in the cgroup shared the CPU while the medians were taken

cross_format.equivalence_reference: py:json reading agent.json; date-times compared as UTC instants, numbers canonically

roundtrip.method: load -> set model.max_tokens = 4096 -> dump, compared with the original file edited by hand on that one line (diff_lines counts +/- lines of a unified diff against that hand edit). The output is re-read: json -> py json (json5 output -> json5), toml -> tomllib, yaml -> 'yaml1.2' = ruamel.yaml safe (1.2 resolver; note it still resolves timestamps and 1_000), 'yaml1.2core' = eemeli yaml 2.9.1 parse (YAML 1.2 core schema, run in the Node probe) and 'yaml1.1' = PyYAML safe_load. hears_as_intended: the re-read data equals agent.json with the edit (what the author meant; date-times compared as instants). same_as_hand_edit_for_reader: the reader hears the same thing in the output as in the hand-edited original. key_order_preserved compares every key path in order.
